bugs.description: The post-login home route is hardcoded to /analytics (src/lib/routes.ts home:'/analytics'), which returns the 404 'Page Not Found' screen for any user who does not have analytics.*. Observed live: QA_AdminLogin_NoModules, QA_GatePassViewer, QA_Mixed and QA_Frontdesk all land on a 404 immediately after a successful login. Also the sidebar/nav hrefs point at /admin/... while the real routes are bare (/ams/..., /analytics); middleware strips /admin, so nav links and deep links are fragile.
bugs.repro: Log in as any user without analytics.* -> redirected to /analytics -> 404.
bugs.fix: Redirect to the first route the user actually has access to (or a neutral landing page), not a fixed /analytics; align nav hrefs with the real route paths.

gaps.detail: Top-nav groups Access Control and Quick Mark are gated by umbrella features appModules.accessControl.* and appModules.quickMark.*, which are separate from the functional module features (employee.*, user.*, etc.). A role granted only functional features sees NO navigation to those modules (confirmed live: QA_HR and QA_Mixed have the module features but an empty top nav).
gaps.impact: Roles must be given the appModules.* umbrella in addition to the module features or users cannot navigate. This is an easy mis-configuration; the RBAC model should either derive group visibility from the child features or document the umbrella requirement clearly.

gaps.detail: Most top-nav groups gate on appModules.* umbrella features, but the Frontdesk group gates directly on visitor.* (navbar-modern.tsx line ~553).
gaps.impact: Inconsistent permission model between modules; Frontdesk behaves differently from Quick Mark / Access Control.

gaps.detail: The admin panel has pages only for AMS (attendance, employee, leave, holiday, shift, unit, attendance-request, system-config), analytics, frontdesk/visitor, and RBAC (user/role/group). There are no admin pages for Customer, Item, or Gate Pass/voucher.
gaps.impact: A voucher-only user (QA_GatePassViewer) has nothing to see or do in the admin panel even though the API exposes those modules.
